news_candidates.title: How AI Is Eroding the First Rung of the Tech Job Ladder
news_candidates.title_zh: How AI Is Eroding the First Rung of the Tech Job Ladder
news_candidates.summary: The US information sector shed roughly 23,000 jobs in August, offering another potential signal of how AI is reshaping the labor market. Northeastern University Professor Alicia Modestino discusses why tech may be the “canary in the coal mine,” with her research showing a decline in junior versus senior software developer vacancies since ChatGPT’s release. She also discusses why employers are demanding more experience, judgment and human-centric skills from entry-level workers. She joins Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

news_candidates.title: US added 162,000 jobs in August, with unemployment rate holding steady
news_candidates.title_zh: US added 162,000 jobs in August, with unemployment rate holding steady
news_candidates.summary: Number of new jobs being added has been fluctuating, with private companies adding 38,000 jobs in August The US economy added 162,000 jobs in August, an uptick after a sluggish summer for the labor market. The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, still down from its most recent peak of 4.5% last November, according to new data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). Despite the relative stability of the unemployment rate, the number of new jobs added to the economy has been fluctuating, going from 214,000 in March down to a 21,000 gain in July and then back up in August. Continue reading...

news_candidates.summary: Diane Swonk, Chief Economist at KPMG, discusses the August jobs report, which showed U.S. payrolls rising by 162,000, above expectations, while the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%. The segment also notes revisions to prior figures and points out that the data contain a lot of noise. She speaks with Scarlet Fu & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

news_candidates.title: Jay Chaudhry Says AI Is Driving More Demand for Cybersecurity at Zscaler
news_candidates.title_zh: Jay Chaudhry Says AI Is Driving More Demand for Cybersecurity at Zscaler
news_candidates.summary: Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry said AI is creating a major tailwind for the cybersecurity industry rather than reducing the need for software security. He argued that CEOs, CIOs, and boards want to use AI for productivity and cost savings, but are worried that new AI models could create vulnerabilities, lead to breaches, or cause applications to be hacked or hijacked. He speaks with Scarlet Fu & Kristine Aquino on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)
